speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing gait and limb ataxia; to better understand your condition given your significant medical history, where exactly do you feel the loss of coordination, and have you noticed any recent changes in your vision or speech?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of appearing "drunk" while walking and right-sided clumsiness suggest significant cerebellar or brainstem involvement. Given your significant medical history, have you experienced any episodes of double vision, difficulty swallowing, or sudden weakness on the right side of your body? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI findings confirm multifocal demyelinating lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leucencephalopathy (PML), which aligns with your right-sided weakness and ataxia. To determine if you have a history of immunosuppression or HIV, which are the primary risk factors for this condition, have you ever been diagnosed with HIV or are you currently taking immunosuppressive medications for an autoimmune disease?

REQUEST TEST: HIV Serology; REQUEST TEST: CD4 Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HIV Serology: Negative. CD4 Count: 500 cells/mm³.

speaker: Doctor
text: The HIV and CD4 count results are normal, which makes PML highly unlikely given the specific MRI description of demyelinating lesions. The clinical picture of subacute ataxia and weakness with multifocal white matter lesions is much more consistent with a demyelinating disease like Multiple Sclerosis. Have you noticed any episodes of transient numbness, visual changes, or bladder dysfunction in the past? REQUEST TEST: Lumbar Puncture for Oligoclonal Bands.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lumbar Puncture Oligoclonal Bands: Positive

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple Sclerosis. The combination of clinical ataxia, right-sided weakness, and the presence of oligoclonal bands in the CSF confirms an inflammatory demyelinating disease. Given the multifocal nature of the symptoms and MRI findings, Multiple Sclerosis is the definitive diagnosis.
